phase: P08 (batch 1: payment records, refunds and payment access)
scope: All 23 payment routes and their guards
application/services/payment.service.ts (create, authorize, capture, refund, void, reads, ownership)
Storefront and admin use of the payment-intent API (none)

findings.problem: Refunds never returned money: the service recorded a refund transaction and tried to cancel the payment, but never called Stripe. The cancel step is not allowed for captured payments, so every refund of a captured payment failed anyway; the refund amount was also unbounded.
findings.change: Refunds of online-provider payments go through the provider (Stripe via a new refund gateway port; other online providers are refused until a gateway exists), recording the provider's refund id; offline payments (cash, bank transfer) are recorded only. The amount is limited to what remains after earlier refunds; payments stay captured, as at the provider.
findings.verification: Unit refunds-and-access: baseline all refund cases failed; fixed Stripe refund issued with the Stripe payment id, partial refunds tracked and over-refunds refused, provider refusal or missing Stripe configuration records nothing, offline refunds recorded.

findings.problem: Payment ownership checks were applied to staff (so staff could not record payments or refund for any customer's order) and were fail-open for customers (skipped for payments not yet attached to an order and for guest orders).
findings.change: Staff and internal callers act without a customer scope; customers may only see or act on payments of orders they own, and anything else is reported as not found.
findings.verification: payment-records E2E: baseline staff got 'Forbidden: you do not own this order' when recording a payment for a customer's order; fixed staff record, process and refund it, the owner reads it, another customer gets 404. Unit cases for own, foreign and guest-order payments.

findings.problem: Any signed-in customer could create payment records for any amount and mark them authorised and captured with a self-supplied reference, fabricating financial records (no frontend uses these routes; customers pay through checkout and Stripe). Refund and void were open to all staff including analysts.
findings.change: Creating and processing payment records is admin-only (offline/manual payments); refunds and voids require ADMIN or CUSTOMER_SERVICE.
findings.verification: E2E: baseline customer created a payment record (201); fixed 403 for create and process.

tests.baseline: With the old service, controller, routes and container: 7 of 8 unit and 2 of 2 E2E cases failed.
tests.database_suites: All E2E and integration suites: 142 tests in 43 files pass
tests.final: 1519 unit tests in 118 files; root/tooling tsc; 7/7 workspace type-checks; API client drift check

follow_ups: Next P08 batch: Stripe create-intent (client-supplied amount, no checkout ownership check), gift cards, promotion usage recording, BNPL, webhook replay protection.
Order refund status (P07) is still set independently of payment refunds; link order refunds to payment refunds.
